newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu leaves France, flies home to crisis.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu leaves France, flies home to crisis.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko left France for his battered homeland on Tuesday after six weeks convalescing on the French Riviera from cancer surgery, witnesses said.

Mobutu's jet took off from Nice airport at 8.50 a.m. (0750 GMT) GMT, headed for Kinshasa. His supporters are preparing a mammoth welcome in Zaire, where Tutsi rebels have seized a swathe of territory in the east of the country.

Mobutu climbed aboard a special DC-8 plane bound for home after arriving at the airport with his entourage in three Mercedes cars, four minibuses and a taxi. Aides were seen loading items such as washing machines and televisions into one of the presidential planes.

Aides of Mobutu, who has been in power in Zaire since 1965, say he is feeling better after surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland in August. He has been staying at his private villa at Roquebrune-cap-Martin near Nice since November 4.
But one Zairean newspaper has said he planned to stay in Zaire just two or three weeks before returning to complete his convalescence in his luxury villa overlooking the Mediterranean.
The rebel coalition has overwhelmed Zaire's ragged army in the east in a two-month offensive, taking several key towns including Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.
